applies_why: Yes: the judge uses the absence of a contrary statement in the text as a reason to label the matter UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
why: The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on the text not stating the contrary, which K-S2 forbids as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
